findings.description: The bucket has no ACL restriction and is documented as public with no bucket policy or public access block restricting it, exposing potentially sensitive data (customer-master.xlsx) to unauthenticated internet access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest, risking exposure of sensitive data if the underlying storage is compromised.
Versioning is not enabled, meaning objects can be overwritten or deleted without recovery, which is a risk for data integrity in combination with the bucket's public exposure.

A sensitive object (customer-master.xlsx, likely containing customer PII) is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket which is publicly accessible and unencrypted, directly exposing sensitive customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket storing financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled for the financials bucket, increasing the risk of irrecoverable data loss or tampering.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in the operations bucket are stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in the data_science bucket are stored unencrypted at rest.
